title: Self-Healing Agentic Orchestrators for Reliable Tool-Augmented Large Language Model Systems
what_it_evaluates: 100-task controlled fault-injection benchmark evaluating monitor-detect-diagnose-recover-verify control loop for tool-augmented LLM agents; measures task success rate under fault injection, single-attempt recovery rate, and silent failure reduction.

title: A Self-Healing Framework for Reliable LLM-Based Autonomous Agents
what_it_evaluates: Multi-agent workflow environments simulating real-world operational scenarios; quantitatively assesses agent reliability, failure taxonomy classification, internal/external failure detection, fault propagation reduction, and adaptive replanning recovery.

title: EvoConfig: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems for Efficient Autonomous Environment Configuration
what_it_evaluates: Automated runtime environment configuration and dependency setup across Repo2Run and Envbench benchmarks; measures configuration success rate, root-cause diagnosis accuracy, and error-fixing recommendations.

title: When Disagreements Elicit Robustness: Investigating Self-Repair Capabilities under LLM Multi-Agent Disagreements
what_it_evaluates: Evaluates emergent self-repair under mild disagreements vs task-critical knowledge conflicts across collaborative reasoning (COUNTERFACT, MQUAKE-CF) and programming (HumanEval, GAIA) benchmarks.

title: Think it, Run it: Autonomous machine learning pipeline generation via self-healing multi-agent artificial intelligence
what_it_evaluates: Automated end-to-end machine learning pipeline generation, execution, and error repair across 150 diverse ML dataset scenarios; measures pipeline completion rate, automated code repair success, and development time reduction.

title: Detecting and Repairing Role Drift in Multi-Agent Collaboration with Lightweight Protocols
what_it_evaluates: Evaluates RoleFix framework on collaborative software engineering and research workflow tasks; measures role-drift incident reduction, task completion rate improvement, and protocol latency overhead.

title: Predictive Self-Healing for Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines Using Model Predictive Control
what_it_evaluates: Evaluates Model Predictive Control (MPC) on multi-agent LLM pipelines for proactive drift anticipation, token budget management, and bottleneck prevention; measures controller cycle latency, MTTR, and pipeline stability.

title: Self-Healing AI Systems using Multi-Agent Learning
what_it_evaluates: Evaluates multi-agent closed-loop observability, diagnosis, and remediation for cloud infrastructure and IoT/smart grid environments; measures incident remediation success, MTTR reduction, and reinforcement learning reward convergence.

title: A survey on Selenium usage, practices, and challenges in end-to-end testing
what_it_evaluates: Empirical industry survey of software testing practitioners analyzing Selenium usage, test flakiness drivers, DOM locator fragility, wait mechanisms, and maintenance costs (qualitative survey, no system benchmark).

title: GUI Agents: A Survey
what_it_evaluates: Comprehensive survey and taxonomy of multimodal GUI agents across web, mobile, and desktop; catalogs benchmark success rates across OSWorld, WebArena, AndroidWorld, Mind2Web; analyzes perception methods, action spaces, and safety risks.

title: From Language Models to Agentic AI: A Survey of Autonomous, Action-Enabled, and Collaborative LLM Agents
what_it_evaluates: Comprehensive survey of autonomous, action-enabled LLM agents; analyzes planning paradigms (ReAct, CoT, ToT), memory architectures (vector, relational), tool interfaces, security risks (privilege escalation, prompt injection), and multi-agent coordination.

title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
what_it_evaluates: Multi-agent conversational orchestration across code generation (HumanEval), math problem solving (MATH), decision making, and web search; evaluates task success rate, conversational turn overhead, token consumption, and human-in-the-loop interaction.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
what_it_evaluates: Interleaved reasoning and action generation evaluated on question answering (HotpotQA, Fever) and interactive decision-making environments (ALFWorld, WebShop); measures task success rate, hallucination rate reduction, and API action step count.

title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
what_it_evaluates: 812 realistic web tasks across 4 live mock domains (e-commerce, social forum, software collaboration/GitLab, CMS); evaluates end-to-end task completion rate, step accuracy, and execution failure modes.

title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents
what_it_evaluates: 220 complex multi-app tasks across 9 simulated daily apps with REST APIs; evaluates task success rate, execution accuracy, and API error handling under interactive coding constraints.

title: VisualWebArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Realistic Visually Grounded Web Tasks
what_it_evaluates: 910 visually grounded web tasks across Classifieds, Shopping, and Reddit; evaluates task success rate, visual locator precision, and visual hallucination errors under multimodal observation.

title: BacktrackAgent: Enhancing GUI Agent with Error Detection and Backtracking Mechanism
what_it_evaluates: Error detection and state-backtracking mechanism on Mobile3M and Auto-UI smartphone/desktop GUI benchmarks; measures task success rate, step-level action accuracy, error recovery rate, and trajectory efficiency.

title: AgentFixer: From Failure Detection to Fix Recommendations in LLM Agentic Systems
what_it_evaluates: 15 failure detectors and 2 root-cause analyzers tested on WebArena and AppWorld; measures failure detection precision/recall, fix recommendation success rate, and performance gain on open models (Mistral/Llama).

title: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)
what_it_evaluates: 2,350 tasks spanning 137 websites and 31 domains; measures Element Selection Accuracy, Action F1, and Step Success Rate across Cross-Task, Cross-Website, and Cross-Domain generalization splits.

title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)
what_it_evaluates: 369 real computer tasks across Ubuntu OS interacting with LibreOffice (Calc, Writer, Impress), Chrome, VS Code, GIMP, VLC, and OS file management; evaluates end-to-end task completion rate, execution duration, and tool call accuracy.
